mainEntity.name: Is LBTT the same as stamp duty in England?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Different statute, different bands and a different surcharge. For England and Northern Ireland use the UK Stamp Duty Calculator.

mainEntity.name: How much is first-time buyer relief in Scotland?

acceptedAnswer.text: It raises the nil-rate band from £145,000 to £175,000 — worth up to £600. There is no £500,000 price cap as in England.

mainEntity.name: What is the Additional Dwelling Supplement?

acceptedAnswer.text: 8% of the whole price, from 5 December 2024, on additional dwellings of £40,000 or more, added on top of the band tax.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the ADS back?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the new home replaces your main residence and you sell the previous one within 36 months of buying the new one. You then claim a repayment from Revenue Scotland.

mainEntity.name: Does this cover a shop or office?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — choose Non-Residential. Slices are 0% to £150,000, 1% to £250,000 and 5% above; ADS is not added. Revenue Scotland's £872,000 office example is £32,100. Lease rent is not calculated.

mainEntity.name: Is this a Revenue Scotland assessment?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Confirm with your solicitor. This page is a planning estimate from published rates.
